First, I'd skip single stack 9mms. They're all the rage right now and the popular ones are generally well made, but personally I think they fit an awkward space between pocket pistols and full size guns with higher capacity. For example, I picked up a PPS M2 awhile back and while it was a fine gun, it's only marginally smaller than the larger PPQ, and when wearing jeans and a t-shirt it was too obvious to wear. If I wanted something that large, I'd rather just get a double stack pistol, have more capacity, and openly carry.

The Walther TPH I got for fun instead ended up being what I actually carried everyday because it's easy to throw in a pocket and so small that I can walk around all day without even thinking about it. I don't have to wear certain clothes, worry about bending over too much, or anything else. A spare mag fits in my coin pocket in my jeans, and if anyone saw it then it would make a nice conversation piece instead of an "omg you have a scary black gun, what are you doing!" type incident. So if you want a small gun for CCW, something newer in 380 or 32 ACP with similar dimensions like the Ruger LCP II is what I'd recommend. Your local gun shop should have some for sale. You can get the Rugers for $300, kel-tecs P32s and such for less ($215-300), and there's some other brands similar to the ruger in 380 but I think they're a little too large. Ruger also has a 22LR version now with a 10+1 round capacity as well, versus 6+1 for the 380. If you're on a tight budget and need experience shooting this might be better because you can buy a lot more ammo for it and practice a lot more with it so that you get better with your gun. It also recoils a ton less, making you more likely to go to the range and practice, and making follow up shots much easier. 22LR is probably the last cartridge you'd want to defend yourself with, but recoil is light and people with 380 pocket pistols seem to never practice with them because they suck to shoot. 22LR inherently has more reliability issues than rimless cartridges, but if you buy CCI minimags and avoid hollowpoints it'll probably be fine. 380 is obviously better for reliability and stopping power, but you lose a few rounds of capacity (10+1 of 22LR vs 6+1 in 380) and it makes small guns a pain to shoot, so if you're just getting into guns and need practice it might be a bad choice.

All that being said, I think Paul Harrell made a good point in his recent video that something that might make sense in normal times, might not make sense in boogaloo times, and times aren't normal right now so things like home invasions with more assailants might be more common. If you're hunkering down at home and aren't going out a lot, then something larger with more capacity would be better. In that case maybe something like a full size double stack glock in 45 ACP would make more sense. Like someone else mentioned, out of favor & rare cartridges are usually still easy to find during times like these. I had no problem getting 6.5 grendel ammunition when 5.56 was all sold out for example, so if you can only find 40 S&W ammo, getting something in that might make the most sense.
